newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan telephone sale postponed again.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan telephone sale postponed again.

text.p: Nicaragua has postponed the scheduled March 31 partial sale of its state telephone company in the hope of better offers at a later date, President Arnoldo Aleman said late on Thursday.

"The privatisation will take place, but we are not in agreement with the offer made. We are not going to sell off the nation's assets to an exclusive concession or at a ridiculous price," Aleman said in government statement.

He said the government, which took power on Jan. 10, was reviewing the privatisation process in which Nicaragua had planned to sell 40 percent of the Empresa Nicaraguense de Telecomunicaciones S.A. (Enitel) to the private sector.
"We are for more openness, without giving monopolies. I don't like state monopolies, because I support free enterprise and I'm not going to permit private monopolies either," he said.
Enitel has officially been on the auction block for almost two years, but Nicaragua has repeatedly postponed its sale because the offers it has received for the firm have been too low.
